title: Bounded-below column-cone spectral sequence for a Cech total map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $u:A^{\bullet,\bullet}\to B^{\bullet,\bullet}$ a morphism of commuting double cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The first index $q$ is the horizontal degree, the second $j$ is the internal degree. Assume $A^{q,j}=B^{q,j}=0$ for $q<0$ or $j<a$, for one integer $a$. Define $\operatorname{Tot}(A)^n=\bigoplus_{q+j=n}A^{q,j}$ and similarly for $B$, with differential $d_h+(-1)^q d_v$; these sums are finite. Form the column cones $C_q=\operatorname{Cone}(u^{q,\bullet})$, with $C_q^j=B^{q,j}\oplus A^{q,j+1}$ and the ordinary cochain cone differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is a convergent column-filtration spectral sequence
$$E_1^{q,j}=H^j(C_q)\quad(q\ge0,\ j\ge a-1)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{q+j}(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(u))).$$
It stabilizes in each bidegree, and its abutment filtration is finite in each total degree [def-sp-spectral-sequence, def-sp-filtration]. Consequently, for every integer $r$, if $H^j(C_q)=0$ for every $q\ge0$ and $j\le r$, then $H^n(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(u)))=0$ for every $n\le r$.

source.place: Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss, finite diagonals (not only nonnegative internal degrees); applied to the double complex of column cones. The signed cone-total identification is spelled out in report.md.

proof.text: Put $b=a-1$ and form $D^{q,j}=B^{q,j}\oplus A^{q,j+1}$ with $d_v(b_0,x)=(d_{B,v}b_0+u x,-d_{A,v}x)$ and $d_h(b_0,x)=(d_{B,h}b_0,d_{A,h}x)$. The cone definition gives $d_v^2=0$; directly, its first component is $d_{B,v}^2b_0+d_{B,v}ux-ud_{A,v}x=0$. Also $d_h^2=0$, and $d_hd_v=d_vd_h$ componentwise because the original differentials commute and $u$ commutes with both. Thus $D$ is a commuting double complex whose column $q$ is $C_q$. It vanishes for $q<0$ or $j<b$, so in total degree $n$ only $0\le q\le n-b$ contribute. Give its finite total the differential $d_h+(-1)^qd_v$ and the decreasing column filtration $F^p\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\bigoplus_{q\ge p}D^{q,n-q}$ as in the cited total-complex definition.

source.place: Definitions definition-double-complex and definition-associated-simple-complex; column filtration in section-double-complex; cone convention in derived.tex, Definition 014E (definition-cone).

proof.text: On the summand $D^{q,j}$, define $T:\operatorname{Tot}(D)\to\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(u))$ by $T(b_0,x)=(b_0,(-1)^q x)$; finite rearrangement of summands identifies the target in degree $n$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^n\oplus\operatorname{Tot}(A)^{n+1}$. This is invertible by the same sign formula and preserves the column filtration. For $b_0$ the differential on both sides is $d_{B,h}b_0+(-1)^qd_{B,v}b_0$. On $x$ the three components of $T d$ are $(-1)^q u x$ in $B^{q,j+1}$, $(-1)^{q+1}d_{A,h}x$ in $A^{q+1,j+1}$, and $-d_{A,v}x$ in $A^{q,j+2}$. The cone differential applied to $T(0,x)$ has exactly these three components, by $d_{\operatorname{Cone}}(b,y)=(d_{\operatorname{Tot}B}b+\operatorname{Tot}(u)y,-d_{\operatorname{Tot}A}y)$. Hence $T$ is an isomorphism of filtered cochain complexes, and identifies their cohomology and image filtrations.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; explicit component calculation using homology.tex, definition-associated-simple-complex.

proof.text: Relabel the internal degree by setting $\widetilde D^{q,k}=D^{q,k+b}$ with the same horizontal and vertical differentials. This is first-quadrant since $q,k\ge0$ on its support. Relabelling, without introducing a cochain-shift sign, identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(\widetilde D)^m$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(D)^{m+b}$ and their differentials and column filtrations, since the total sign depends only on $q$. Apply the first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to $\widetilde D$ in the abelian category of $\Lambda$-modules. Its first page is $\widetilde E_1^{q,k}=H^k(\widetilde D^{q,\bullet})=H^{k+b}(C_q)$ and it converges to $H^{q+k+b}(\operatorname{Tot}(D))$. Write $j=k+b$, and use $T$ from step 2, to obtain exactly the asserted spectral sequence and abutment. The same theorem gives stabilization for page index $s>\max(q,j-b+1)$ and the finite image filtration: in total degree $n\ge b$, $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n-b+1}H^n=0$. For $n<b$ the total degree-$n$ term is zero, so its cohomology and entire filtration are zero. Thus convergence and finiteness hold for every integer $a$ and every total degree.

source.place: Tags 0130 (lemma-ss-double-complex) and 0132 (lemma-first-quadrant-ss), applied after the explicit translation j=k+(a-1).

proof.text: Assume the column-cone vanishing through $r$ and fix $n\le r$. For every $q\ge0$ on the total-degree-$n$ diagonal, $j=n-q\le r$, so $E_1^{q,n-q}=0$; entries outside the support also vanish. By the spectral-sequence page rule $E_{s+1}=H(E_s)$, a zero entry remains zero on the next page (its kernel is zero and its incoming image is a submodule of zero), hence on every later page and at stabilization. Convergence from step 3 identifies each $F^qH^n/F^{q+1}H^n$ with this zero stable entry. A finite filtration with all successive quotients zero has equal consecutive steps; its zero end therefore equals its whole-module end. Thus $H^n(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(u)))=0$ for every $n\le r$.
